about: World Pulse data. One entry per running story (thread), each with a dated log of updates. Add to it, never rewrite history: new facts go in as a new update. Run build_pulse.py after editing.

threads.title: Starship Flight 15

updates.text: Launched from Starbase. Booster 22 turned back for a tower catch, found a guidance problem, diverted over the Gulf and broke apart just before the water. Ship 42 reached orbit.

Ship 42 is still in orbit about 275 km up. It released 26 Starlink satellites and passed health checks over Hawaii and Chile. Final check about 2:29 pm Eastern; tower catch planned about 4:20 pm Eastern.
One live blog (drohnen.de) says a ship engine failed and the flight was cut to 3 hours. Nobody else reports it.
Ship 42 came home and was caught by the tower's arms at Starbase. It is the first time SpaceX has caught a Starship upper stage back from orbit. The flight lasted about 22 and a half hours.
The drohnen.de claim of a ship engine failure and a 3 hour flight is contradicted. CNBC reports the ship circled the Earth 14 times before landing on the tower.

Recaps say Ship 42 was caught about 22 hours 33 minutes after liftoff, after 14 orbits. Booster 22 called off its own catch and came down in the Gulf of Mexico. No date for Flight 16 has been announced.

No Flight 16 date yet. NASASpaceFlight says December is the aim, possibly the first Starship launch from pad 39A in Florida, with Booster 23 and Ship 43. Some sites now say early 2027. Musk says losing Booster 22 does not change the plan.

Still no Flight 16 date. It is aimed at no earlier than December 2026, from pad 39A in Florida, and no launch licence had been announced as of 16 Nov. Musk says the next flight will try to catch both the ship and the booster. He also describes a bigger next version (V4), about 70 metres tall with over 60% more fuel.

threads.title: US flights halted nationwide

updates.text: The FAA halted every US departure after a communications failure hit the en-route control centres. About 1.5 million travellers stranded. Homeland Security: no sign of an attack.
Flights back after about 4 hours (3:54 to 8:15 pm Eastern); over 15,000 flights hit. Cause still disputed: overloaded routers or system updates, depending on which official is speaking.

The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) says the root cause is still unknown. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy says it began while a contractor, L3Harris, moved old copper phone lines to fiber; L3Harris says it is helping the investigation. Officials say there is no sign of a cyberattack. Saturday cancellations passed 5,000.

The Federal Aviation Administration's (FAA) first review points to two sites: a radio site in El Dorado, Arkansas, where L3Harris was installing a new router, and a radar site in Amarillo, Texas. Blocking both calmed the network. The FAA has switched off a broadcasting feature on all the new routers. Officials still do not say whether it was human error or a faulty router. Flights were close to normal by Sunday.

Monday morning: 284 US flights cancelled and 954 delayed (FlightAware), mostly American Airlines. Since Friday the total is about 18,520 cancelled and over 28,300 delayed. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy repeated on Sunday there is no sign of a cyberattack.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy says a router is the "likely cause"; a Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) team is at contractor L3Harris's lab in Florida, and he asked the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) to help. Juniper Networks, maker of the Arkansas router, says its device "did not fail". Duffy repeated his ask for $50 billion; Senators Jack Reed, Ted Cruz and leader John Thune questioned the number. Flighty counts over 17,000 cancellations Friday to Sunday, the worst technology-caused disruption on record. Monday: 347 cancelled by 6 pm.

The Wall Street Journal reports (as quoted by other outlets) that the Arkansas unit was a new Juniper router installed by L3Harris, and officials believe a feature that broadcast data too widely caused the overload. Duffy says a second router, in Amarillo, Texas, then flooded the network. Engineers from the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), Juniper and Cisco are testing the equipment in Florida. The FAA has not given a final cause and no cyberattack has been found.

threads.title: Microsoft 365 outage

updates.text: Outlook, Teams and Copilot down in 74+ countries. Microsoft: no sign of an attack. It also knocked out Claude logins for 2 hours on 13 Nov.
Services back. Still no root cause: reports differ between a network change, a capacity upgrade and servers failing health checks.
Nothing new from Microsoft found in major outlets.
Nothing new from Microsoft found. No new outage confirmed on 15 Nov.
Third scan with nothing new. Marked as gone quiet.

threads.title: Iran presses on US bases

updates.text: The US moved tanker aircraft and Ospreys out of RAF Mildenhall in England over a reported Iranian threat. Bases raised to a higher protection level.
US forces shot down 2 Iranian drones aimed at Bahrain, home of the US Fifth Fleet. First Iranian shot at a Gulf base in two months. No damage.
Iran calls it payback for a US strike in southern Iran and claims it hit a US radar; the US denies it. No US strike back found.

Second attack on Bahrain in three days. Iran's Revolutionary Guards say six drones went for a US air defence radar at the Al-Riffa helicopter base. Bahrain sounded its first nationwide alert since September and says it shot the attack down. No damage or casualties reported; no US statement yet. Saudi Arabia also reported Houthi missiles aimed at Riyadh, intercepted.

The US military gives a different count for Sunday's attack on Bahrain: it says the Revolutionary Guards launched two one-way attack drones, not six, and US forces shot both down. Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Jordan and Egypt condemned Iran.

Third claimed attack on Bahrain in five days. Iran's Revolutionary Guards say their drones hit a US-run radar at Sheikh Isa Air Base, saying US drones keep crossing into Iranian airspace. Bahrain sounded a shelter alert and explosions were heard over Manama. Bahrain's armed forces say they destroyed the attackers before they reached their target. No US statement found yet. Separately, a third US aircraft carrier, the USS Theodore Roosevelt, is now in the region; US Central Command (CENTCOM) calls it a scheduled rotation. Qatar urged all sides to hold back.

threads.title: Strait of Hormuz: tankers hit, oil up

updates.text: Explosions hit 4 oil tankers in the strait. Brent crude near $94 a barrel.
Ship traffic is a trickle: about 3 ships a day against 85 before the war. Oil near $96. Iran says the tankers ignored warnings (not verified).
Brent crude closed Friday at $95.84 a barrel. Traders will react when futures reopen Sunday evening.
Iran's Revolutionary Guards say three oil tankers hit sea mines in the strait and caught fire. The ships were not named and nobody has verified it. The US says the main routes are cleared of mines.

Iran's Revolutionary Guards now say two more tankers hit mines on Monday 16 Nov, and that one supertanker carrying over two million barrels sank. Iran's count is six tankers in two days. None of it is verified and no ship has been named. US Central Command (CENTCOM) says the strait has been swept clear.

More ship damage reported by an independent monitor. The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre (UKMTO) reported on 16 Nov a tanker hit by an "unknown projectile" with an engine room fire, crew safe, and later a disabled tanker with an engine room fire north of Khasab, Oman. UKMTO named neither ship. Iran's Guards claim yet another mine hit on Tuesday morning, with no evidence. Iran's mine story and its count of six or more tankers are still unproven, and the US says the shipping lanes are clear. Iran and Oman's foreign ministers met in Muscat about keeping ships safe.

threads.title: Drones over RAF Lakenheath

updates.text: Suspected drones over the US base; it sheltered in place. Link to Iran not proven.
UK Ministry of Defence says it is resolved, no damage. One outlet says Russia was behind it; nobody else confirms.
Nothing new found.
Nothing new found. Nobody has been named as responsible.
Third scan with nothing new. Marked as gone quiet.

threads.title: Ukraine war: Moscow airports shut by drones

updates.text: Strikes both ways: blackouts in Ukraine, drones over Moscow.
All four Moscow airports shut. Moscow's mayor says more than 100 drones were shot down (Russian figure, not verified).

Zelenskyy says US negotiators asked whether Ukraine would leave Donbas in return for joining NATO (the North Atlantic Treaty Organization). The US has not confirmed it; the Kremlin has not answered. Zelenskyy says any land deal would go to a national vote. Russia sent 117 drones at Ukraine overnight, killing at least two.

More detail on the Abu Dhabi talks: they ended without a breakthrough, but both sides agreed a prisoner swap of more than 1,000 people. Zelenskyy says Ukraine proposed a local truce for seven or eight front line villages where civilians are trapped.

Russia's defence ministry says it downed 1,336 Ukrainian drones over 16 regions, the most in one night of the war (Russian figure). Crimea's Russian-installed governor says the bridge to Crimea was hit; the Kremlin calls the damage minor and road traffic was halted for repairs. Refineries and industrial sites were also hit; six people injured in Ilsky. Zelenskyy says the refinery strikes cut over half of Russia's refining capacity (not verified). Ukraine has not commented on the bridge.

Ukraine's General Staff says its drones hit the Ilsky oil refinery in southern Russia. The Crimean Bridge was shut to vehicles, then partly reopened. One Ukrainian outlet (UA News) says Russia now claims 1,441 drones downed; not confirmed elsewhere, and all Russian counts are unverified. Russia hit a cardboard factory in Odesa with a jet drone.

threads.title: UK: US Army officer held over Russia spying

updates.text: A US lieutenant colonel at a NATO corps was caught in a UK sting, suspected of trying to spy for Russia. Officials say it is separate from the Iran threats.
Nothing new found.

Reports name the officer as Lieutenant Colonel Brandon Tyner, a senior personnel officer at the NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organization) corps headquarters at Imjin Barracks. He has not been charged. The Kremlin denies any part in it.
Nothing new surfaced in this scan.

threads.title: Bitcoin slides as bond rates jump

updates.text: Bitcoin under $70,000 and US stocks slid after a hot inflation report. $1.3 billion in crypto bets wiped out.
Bitcoin near $68,000, lowest since August. US 10-year bond rate hit 5.13%.
Bitcoin kept falling on Saturday, touching about $63,300, its lowest since mid-August. The 10-year bond rate ended Friday near 5.13%.
Bitcoin dipped to about $62,000 over the weekend, then climbed back to about $65,000 on Monday. Crypto trade sites point to money leaving Bitcoin funds and fear of higher interest rates.
Bitcoin slipped back to about $64,000 (Fortune: $64,013 at 7:30 am Eastern on Monday). It was near $64,200 early Tuesday as US stock futures pointed lower before Nvidia's results.

threads.title: Nvidia boss Jensen Huang resigns

updates.text: Resigned effective immediately (company filing). Finance chief Colette Kress is interim chief executive. Shares fell as much as 13%, then bounced.
Nothing new found.
Nothing new dated this weekend.

The Financial Times reports Jensen Huang is talking with allies about coming back as chief executive; one ally describes a 'war room' of tech bosses. Neither Huang nor Nvidia has confirmed. Shares slipped about 2% before the market opened on Monday.

Reports say the board is not considering bringing Jensen Huang back. The Commerce Department issued a rule requiring a licence to send advanced chips to Brazil, Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand, to stop Chinese firms renting that computing power through data centres there. Nvidia fell about 4% to its lowest close since July 2025. Its quarterly results are due Tuesday 17 Nov.

Nvidia shares fell about 4% on Monday to their lowest close since July 2025 (CNBC). Reports still say the board is not considering bringing Huang back; an online petition for his return passed 190,000 signatures. Results come out after the market closes today, the first without Huang. Interim chief executive Colette Kress, the finance chief, leads. Analysts expect revenue near $109 billion.

next.what: Nvidia results, after the US market closes (about 4:20 pm Eastern is usual; exact time not confirmed)

threads.title: Ebola in Congo

updates.text: About 11,000 cases and 5,300+ deaths. Cases also seen in Uganda, Kenya, Nigeria and France.
Still 400 to 500 new cases a week, slowing in some areas. Armed groups are holding back the response; a nurse was killed. Kenya has started its 42-day countdown to being declared free.

Over 11,000 confirmed cases and about 5,430 deaths (European health agency figures to 10 Nov). Six months in, the Washington Post says it is still out of control and could pass the death toll of the West Africa outbreak. There is no approved vaccine for this strain (Bundibugyo).

New US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) figures to 12 Nov: 11,285 confirmed cases and 5,509 deaths. The United Nations says armed groups attacking civilians and health workers are holding back the response.

Newest European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) figures, to 14 Nov: 11,376 confirmed cases and 5,568 deaths. The CDC calls it the second largest Ebola outbreak on record. It still says the risk to the US public is low, with no US cases.

threads.title: New Orleans: tanker rams a river cruise ship

updates.text: A tanker hit a docked cruise ship under the Crescent City Connection bridge. 32 people to hospital, none critical. The mayor says the tanker lost control; investigation open.

National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) investigators recovered the tanker's voyage data recorder; a 16 person team will spend about a week there. The NTSB says it is too early to know the cause; the Coast Guard mentions a possible loss of steering. All 197 people survived. The port has sued to hold the tanker, Atlantic Asphalt. The cruise ship is still on its side.

National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) officials say the early finding is a steering failure that disabled the tanker's rudder. The Atlantic Asphalt dropped anchors and radioed warnings before it hit the docked American Heritage. The NTSB says the investigation is only beginning.
Nothing new surfaced in this scan.

threads.title: Washington DC: shooting at a gym

updates.text: A gunman killed a building manager; four to six others hurt. Police say it followed a long dispute with his building. Casualty counts still differ between outlets.

Police named the gunman as Matt Wade Lambert, 55, who lived in the building; he was found dead of a self-inflicted wound. The man killed was the building manager, James Stuart, 46. Outlets still differ on whether four or five people were hurt.
Nothing new found.
Nothing new surfaced in this scan.

threads.title: Trump, Putin and Xi to meet in China

updates.text: News summaries say the three leaders may meet at the summit in Shenzhen, with the Iran war and nuclear weapons on the agenda. Not yet confirmed by the governments.

Now confirmed by the White House and the Kremlin: Trump, Xi and Putin will meet on Thursday 19 November in Shenzhen, on the side of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit. Trump wants to talk about nuclear weapons; a US official says not to expect a deal. North Korea and the Iran war may also come up.

China's foreign ministry now confirms it too, so all three governments agree: Thursday 19 Nov in Shenzhen. Trump is expected to see Xi one to one first. A Kremlin aide says no separate Putin and Trump meeting has been agreed.

Trump landed in Manila for a state visit, a special summit with the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN), and a Quad meeting (the US, India, Japan and Australia), before going on to Shenzhen. Protesters marched against the Iran war; one report says hundreds have been arrested since 15 Nov. Accounts still differ on a separate Trump and Putin meeting: the Kremlin says yes, a US official says none is scheduled. The APEC leaders' meeting runs 18 to 19 Nov.

next.what: Trump, Xi and Putin meet in Shenzhen (day set, hour not announced; countdown is to the start of 19 Nov in China)

threads.title: Fedwire and 911 problems (claims only)

updates.text: One tracker claims a Federal Reserve wire system disruption; one outlet reports 911 call problems from 298 user reports. The Fed shows normal operations.
Still a single source each. No major outlet or official confirms either.
Still a single source each (Cybernews for the 911 reports). No official confirms either.
Third scan with nothing new. Still a single source each. Marked as gone quiet.
Still quiet. Nothing new.

threads.title: US West Coast: atmospheric river storms

updates.text: A run of storms fed by an atmospheric river (a long band of moist air) is bringing rain, mountain snow and big waves to the West Coast. Forecasters warn of flooding near wildfire burn scars, especially in northwest Washington. No damage reports found yet.

Two more atmospheric rivers hit Oregon and Washington back to back on Friday and Saturday, after two earlier in the week. Coastal flood advisories covered Olympia, Seattle and Everett. No major flood damage found in reports so far.
Nothing new surfaced in this scan.

threads.title: Vulcan rocket lost with 40 Amazon satellites

updates.text: United Launch Alliance (ULA) launched its Vulcan rocket from Cape Canaveral with 40 Amazon Leo internet satellites. ULA says an anomaly hit about 10 minutes into flight and the satellites never reached orbit. It is ULA's first total failure since the company began in 2006. The cause is not known; engine maker Blue Origin is helping, and NASA (the National Aeronautics and Space Administration) has offered help.

No cause yet. Reports say the US Space Force has paused Vulcan for national security launches until the cause is found and fixed, and that Blue Origin, which makes the first stage engines, is helping the investigation (Reuters, as quoted by others). Amazon's 38-launch deal with ULA stands. Amazon's next Leo launch is on a European Ariane 6, no earlier than 23 Nov.

next.what: Amazon Leo satellites launch on an Ariane 6 from French Guiana (no earlier than; day only)

threads.title: Houthi missiles fired at Riyadh

updates.text: The Saudi-led coalition says it shot down two ballistic missiles fired by the Houthis in Yemen at Riyadh, plus three drones over the Eastern Province. No casualties reported. The US Embassy issued a nationwide security alert on Saturday.

Gulf News says Saudi Arabia stopped six drones and two ballistic missiles aimed at Mecca, Medina, Riyadh and the Eastern Province on 15 Nov. The Houthis say Saudi strikes killed or wounded 37 people in Yemen in 24 hours (their figure; Saudi Arabia did not comment). Saudi Arabia named a new commander for its coalition in Yemen after Yemeni government forces fell back toward Aden.

threads.title: Gaza: Israel kills a Hamas commander

updates.text: An Israeli strike in Mawasi, Khan Younis killed Samir Abu Younis, head of Hamas's Rafah Brigade. Israel and Hamas both confirm his death. He had led the brigade for about two months, since his predecessor was killed. Others were wounded; counts differ.
Nothing new surfaced in this scan.

threads.title: Amazon cloud sign-in outage (reports)

updates.text: Tech news sites say Amazon Web Services (AWS) had about three hours of sign-in and connection trouble in its Northern Virginia region, now fixed. Only seen on tech trade sites; not checked against AWS itself or a major outlet. No sign of an attack reported.
Nothing new. Still only on tech trade sites.

threads.title: US bank apps and websites down

updates.text: Online banking failed for customers of Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, U.S. Bank and Truist. Chase had the most complaints, nearly 4,800 on the outage tracker Downdetector by 2 pm. Chase says it is a software bug in its own in-house hardware, not a cyberattack. Wells Fargo says online banking is unavailable and points people to cash machines, branches and phone banking. Zelle (the bank-to-bank payment app) says its own network is fine; delays come from the banks. Capital One says it is not affected. Not fixed as of 4:28 pm Eastern; Chase aims to fix it by end of day. No bank has said the other banks share the same cause.

Chase says "transactions are now posting normally"; customers kept access to their money throughout, though some payments were slow. No all-clear found yet from Wells Fargo. Correction to the earlier entry: the start time is not confirmed. NBC News says only that it began Monday morning; the "about 9 am" figure was when one outlet started counting complaints, not a confirmed start.

Outage trackers showed service back to normal early Tuesday (Downdetector figures quoted by CoinCentral, not a bank statement). Wells Fargo, Bank of America, PNC and U.S. Bank each say their own systems were not the source; some of their customers saw delays on transfers involving Chase. Chase blames a technical bug, not a cyberattack. No full cause given.

threads.title: US loses measles elimination status

updates.when: Decided last week, reported 14 to 16 Nov
updates.text: The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO), the World Health Organization office for the Americas, found measles has spread in the US without a break for more than a year. That ends the elimination status the US has held since 2000, the first loss in 26 years. Cases this year are more than double last year. Death counts differ by source (6 confirmed by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), at least 10 from state reports). Experts say getting the status back could take many months.
Nothing new surfaced in this scan.

threads.title: Two planes collide while taxiing in Miami

updates.text: The wingtip of a Copa Airlines Boeing 737 (166 passengers, 6 crew) hit the nose of a UPS Boeing 767 cargo jet as both taxied, the day after the nationwide ground stop. Two people had minor injuries, treated at the scene. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) says controllers had told the UPS crew to give way. The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) is investigating.
Nothing new surfaced in this scan.

threads.title: Alaska elects a Democratic governor

updates.text: Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins won outright with 50.8% of first-choice votes, so no ranked-choice count was needed. Trump-backed Republican Bernadette Wilson had 28.1% and conceded; three Republicans split the vote. First Democrat to win since Tony Knowles in 1998; at 37 he will be the youngest governor in Alaska history.

Checked: his state election filing lists his age as 37 (born 7 Feb 1989). The "youngest governor in Alaska history" line comes from Alaska Public Media; no other source checked here names the previous youngest.
Nothing new surfaced in this scan.

threads.title: United Airlines computer outage holds flights

updates.text: United reported a "widespread system outage" that kept departing flights at the gate, three days after the nationwide ground stop. Fixed about an hour later. United says flights in the air and United Express were not affected and there is no sign of a cyberattack; no link to Friday has been shown. Over 590 United flights were delayed on Monday; how many came from the outage is unclear.
Nothing new surfaced in this scan.

threads.title: Wall Street selloff led by chip stocks

updates.text: Dow down 739 points (1.41%) to 51,608; S&P 500 down 1.92% to 7,417; Nasdaq down 2.49% to 24,510, about 11% below its 6 October high (a "correction"). Reasons given: Nvidia's leadership turmoil, the new chip export rule, and caution before Nvidia's results on Tuesday and Anthropic's expected stock market listing on Thursday.
Dow and S&P 500 futures pointed lower before Tuesday's open, ahead of Nvidia's results after the close (Benzinga).

threads.title: Report: Iran drawing up dirty bomb options for Washington

updates.text: CNN, citing seven US officials, reports that US intelligence shows Iran developing plans for a possible "dirty bomb" (an ordinary bomb packed with radioactive material) or chemical attack aimed at senior Trump administration officials in Washington. Sources describe it as Iran giving itself options, not an imminent attack, and are split on whether Iran has people in place. The White House says it is "monitoring any and all potential threats, but at this time there are no credible threats to the homeland." Iran's United Nations mission called the chemical weapons claim "wholly illegitimate" and did not address the dirty bomb part. No Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) or DC police statement, device or security change found. Single original source (CNN); other outlets repeat it. A separate claim of a "credible" car bomb threat on Washington traced back to a 2011 photo caption and is not current.

White House spokesperson Lauren Bis again says there are "no credible threats to the homeland". An official describes Iran's planning as building options, not an imminent attack. Still one original source (CNN); no device, arrest or security change found.

threads.title: Phuket: building fire kills 11

updates.when: 16 Nov, early hours local (Sunday afternoon Eastern)
updates.text: A fire tore through a four storey commercial building in Patong, killing 11 people and injuring 16. Police say an electric transformer outside blew and set the fuel pump of a motorcycle rental shop alight; investigators are still confirming the cause. Victims seem to have fled upward to escape. Reports say no tourists were among the dead.

threads.title: Magnitude 6.6 earthquake, Banda Sea, Indonesia
threads.place: Banda Sea, west of Tual, Indonesia

updates.text: The US Geological Survey (USGS) recorded a magnitude 6.6 earthquake under the sea 148 km west-southwest of Tual, Indonesia. It shows no tsunami flag and a green alert, meaning little damage expected. No damage or injury reports found. The only magnitude 6 or bigger quake in the last day.

threads.title: Anthropic stock market debut expected

next.what: Anthropic shares expected to start trading (reported, not confirmed by the company; day only)

updates.text: Reports say the artificial intelligence company Anthropic will set its share price on Wednesday 18 Nov and start trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday 19 Nov, at a value of about $1.4 trillion. The Wall Street Journal says 19 or 20 Nov. The company has not confirmed a date, and earlier talk of 16 Nov passed with no listing.
